subject: Pricing & traffic allocation — quick recap + next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@hummingbird.health>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & traffic allocation — quick recap + next steps

Alex — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. Short version up front: you said Hummingbird is targeting ~10M tokens/month initially with the ability to scale to ~40M over 6–12 months, and you’re aiming for a blended target spend near $1,000 / 1M tokens (give-or-take). Below are the assumptions I captured and a proposed split for routing/traffic that will help hit your unit economics goals.

1) Confirmed ask / constraints
- Expected starting volume: ~10M tokens/month (prod), 30–40M longer-term with pilot->GA.
- Budget target: ~ $900–1,100 per 1M tokens (customer target = $1,000 / 1M tokens).
- Hard requirement: PII data stays in VPC; you requested isolated routing for PHI paths.

2) Proposed model mix (blended routing to meet $/1M target)
- Chat (instruction + responses): 60% of tokens
- Embeddings (vector store indexing / semantic search): 30% of tokens
- Rerank / lightweight ranker calls: 10% of tokens

3) Per-call token assumptions (average) — lets us convert per-request to token volumes
- Chat: 700 tokens (prompt + reply)
- Embeddings: 200 tokens per text unit (batched internally)
- Rerank: 150 tokens

4) Unit economics (blended example at customer target $1,000 / 1M tokens)
- At 10M tokens/mo -> estimated spend = $10,000/mo (blended).
- With the above split, we can tune batching and KV caching on chat paths to reduce per-token cost by ~7–12% vs naive routing.

5) Next steps / asks from you
- Please confirm the 10M starting volume and whether the 30–40M longer-term is a hard target or an upper bound.
- Confirm whether embeddings will be used for both search and semantic-match (affects batching and hardware selection).
- If you’re comfortable, approve the attached routing CSV (redwood-routing-proposal.csv) which outlines the per-endpoint split we’ll test in the pilot.

What I’ll do next: Vanessa will draft a formal quote & three-month pilot pricing band based on two commitment options (month-to-month pilot vs 12-month commitment), and I’ll share a recommended routing configuration that minimizes cost while meeting your latency SLAs.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a quick follow-up if you want to run the numbers live.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

Attachments: redwood-routing-proposal.csv (CSV: endpoint, percent_traffic, model_family, notes)
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@hummingbird.health>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pricing & traffic allocation — quick recap + next steps

Thanks Rachel — that captures the call well. A couple of clarifications from our side before we commit to the routing CSV: 

- The 30–40M is our scaling target if pilot results are good; 10M is the conservative production expectation for Q3.
- Embeddings will be used for both search and short-form recommendations (so we'd expect a mix of large-batch indexing jobs + smaller per-query embedding calls).
- Our internal procurement wants a target blended $/1M token price but also needs a line-item view by model family for forecasting (embeddings vs chat vs rerank).

Two asks: 
1) Can you provide a sample per-model price table you’d expect to apply to the blended $/1M? e.g., Chat = $X / 1M, Embeddings = $Y / 1M, Rerank = $Z / 1M (we understand these will be blended/routed automatically).
2) What are the expected savings if we enable aggressive KV caching on chat (we called this out as important for latency-sensitive flows)?

Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to have a PO in ~2 weeks if pricing and security look good.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Chen
Head of AI Platforms, Hummingbird Health
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@hummingbird.health>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 18:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pricing & traffic allocation — quick recap + next steps

Alex — thanks, great questions. Below is the per-model breakout we suggest for forecasting + two pilot pricing bands you can review with procurement. I’ve attached a draft quote (Redwood-quote-draft.pdf) and the routing CSV for the pilot.

Per-model indicative rates (blended equivalents; final numbers depend on commit/term):
- Chat (large LM family, optimized kernels + batching): $1,400 / 1M tokens (list)
- Embeddings (vector encoder; heavy batching savings possible): $500 / 1M tokens (list)
- Rerank (small autoregressive / optimized): $300 / 1M tokens (list)

Blended examples at 10M tokens / month (using the earlier 60/30/10 split):
- Weighted blended rate = 0.6*1400 + 0.3*500 + 0.1*300 = $1,030 / 1M tokens (list)
- Estimated monthly invoice (no commit discounts) = 10 * $1,030 = $10,300 / month

Pilot pricing bands we can offer (subject to SOW & minimal security review):
A) Month-to-month pilot (no long-term commitment): blended $1,030 / 1M tokens; pilot surcharge for isolated PHI routing + retention controls = +8% for the pilot period.
B) 12‑month commit (tiered): starting blended $950 / 1M tokens, drops to $900 / 1M at >=25M tokens sustained monthly for 3 months.

KV caching note: enabling aggressive KV/prefix caching for sessioned chat traffic typically reduces billable tokens on chat by ~8–15% depending on prompt reuse. For your workload (dialog with frequent reuse of system prompts and repeated user intents), we estimate conservative ~9% token reduction on chat paths if caching rules are applied and TTLs are tuned. That translates to ~5–6% reduction on blended spend at the 60/30/10 mix.

Next steps (I’ll action these today):
- Vanessa will generate a formal quote PDF + a short SOW describing PHI routing and retention controls (you’ll get it as Redwood-quote-draft.pdf).
- Sergio will prepare a brief security addendum template for your InfoSec (SOC2 artifacts + network diagram).
- If you confirm the 10M start number, we’ll produce a test routing config in the attached CSV for an initial 2-week A/B run to validate latency and cost.

Can you confirm the 10M starting volume and which pilot option (A or B) you prefer? If procurement needs an explicit vendor PO template, we can share ours to speed things up.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
